scenes.headline: How Gigatoken tokenizes text at gigabytes per second
scenes.sub: A drop-in tokenizer: a SIMD scanner instead of a regex, plus a word cache.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Papaya! Before a model sees a token, terabytes of text must become numbers. Here's how Gigatoken does it at gigabytes a second.

scenes.text: The win isn't more threads. Gigatoken replaces the regex pretokenizer with a SIMD scanner, and caches every word it has already encoded.
scenes.mark: caches every word it has already encoded
scenes.say: The idea: the win isn't more threads. Replace the regex with a SIMD scanner, and cache every word already encoded.

left.title: HuggingFace and tiktoken
items: A big regex over every byte
left.say: HuggingFace and tiktoken are already multithreaded Rust. So the speedup can't come from switching languages.

right.title: Gigatoken
right.say: It comes from the algorithm: rewrite the hot loop for the hardware, and stop re-encoding words you've seen.

scenes.title: Where the time goes, and where it went

steps.note: usually a regex: most of the wall-clock
steps.say: A tokenizer first splits text into word-ish chunks. Almost everyone runs a big regex for that, and it's most of the wall-clock.
Gigatoken makes the exact same split with a hand-written SIMD scanner, at over two gigabytes a second per thread.
Every chunk checks a cache first. Real text is mostly repeated words, so it hits constantly, and a hit is just a lookup.
Only a word it hasn't encoded yet runs the BPE merges.

scenes.label: GPT-2 on a 12 GB file on an M4 Max; HuggingFace does 6.2 MB/s
scenes.say: On an M4 Max laptop, the GPT-2 tokenizer runs at eight point two seven gigabytes a second. HuggingFace does six point two megabytes.

scenes.label: to tokenize all of Common Crawl, about 130 trillion tokens, on a 144-core EPYC
scenes.note: SentencePiece tokenizers gain only ~10-20x: that path isn't optimized yet
scenes.say: On a big server chip, all of Common Crawl, about a hundred and thirty trillion tokens, takes just under six and a half hours.

scenes.text: Already optimized is not optimal: the hot loop was a regex nobody had rewritten for the hardware.

recap: A SIMD scanner replaces the regex split
A cache turns seen words into lookups
scenes.say: To recap: a scanner instead of a regex, a cache for words already seen, and tokenizing at disk speed.
